def _safe_div(a: pd.Series, b: pd.Series) -> pd.Series:
    """Element-wise division that survives zero denominators.

    V7 DD-1 / Wave-24 (2026-05-03): the previous implementation
    `a / b.replace(0, 1e-10)` collapsed `0/0` to `0`. Combined with
    `(1 - _safe_div(...)).clip(0, 1)`, this produced a SATURATED
    score (1.0) on flat-price / warmup / halted bars — the platform
    manufactured synthetic "high breakout score" out of zero signal.
    Now: when BOTH a and b are ~0 at the same index, the result is
    NaN, which downstream `.fillna(0.0)` converts to a clean 0
    (no signal → no score). Non-zero numerator over zero denominator
    still uses the 1e-10 epsilon (same legacy semantics for those).
    """
    a_zero = a.abs() < 1e-12
    b_zero = b.abs() < 1e-12
    raw = a / b.replace(0, 1e-10)
    # Mark 0/0 explicitly as NaN so callers don't propagate phantom values.
    return raw.where(~(a_zero & b_zero), other=float("nan"))
limitations: Synthetic mechanics and causal counterfactual only; no profitability/edge or September24 lost-trade claim.
Existing synchronous next-open fills with class spread and5bp slippage; no exchange queue, latency or partial fill model.
Same fixed pre-existing W100 capital/history/throttle fixture, not the deployed account.
Historical bars only; live subscription/sparse-feed behavior belongs to separate integration tests.
Candidate/gate counts are repeated per-tick evaluations, not unique opportunities or ordered exclusive funnels.
Repeat equality excludes random order/lifetime/client IDs and wall performance telemetry; preserves ordered decisions, quantities, fills, simulated timestamps, position ledger, equity and risk.
